name: Bujumbura
subtitle: Bujumbura, capital of Burundi: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: Bujumbura was founded as a German colonial garrison town in 1897.
EBSCO dates the German colonial outpost more loosely, between 1889 and 1899 (sources differ on the exact year).

parts.text: Bujumbura was founded as a German colonial garrison town in 1897.
EBSCO dates the German colonial outpost more loosely, between 1889 and 1899 (sources differ on the exact year).
Belgium took control in 1916, during the First World War, and made Bujumbura a military post.
Burundi became independent in 1962 (EBSCO says the Tutsi minority then gained control of the government).
In December 2018 the Burundian authorities adopted a bill fixing the political capital in Gitega and the economic capital in Bujumbura (AFP report).

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in Bujumbura?

parts.text: 1,207,000 in 2023, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: EBSCO gives 'roughly 1.207 million (2023 estimate)' and does not define the boundary (city proper vs wider area).

items.text: Bujumbura (then Usumbura) is founded as a German colonial garrison town.
Belgium takes control and makes Bujumbura a military post.
The town has between 2,500 and 3,000 inhabitants and is predominantly Muslim, per Castryck.
A fire destroys much of the Central Market, noticed at 6:30 a.m. on a Sunday; only 10% of 5,000 merchants had insured goods.
Authorities adopt a bill making Gitega the political capital and Bujumbura the economic capital.
